newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sends $100,000 to Iran quake victims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sends $100,000 to Iran quake victims.

text.p: The United States announced on Monday it would contribute $100,000 to help victims of the earthquake in Iran but denied this signalled any change in policy toward the fundamentalist regime there.
Secretary of State Madeleine Albright "has decided that the United States will extend roughly $100,000 in emergency humanitarian assistance," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
He said he expected the assistance would be funnelled through the International Federation of the Red Cross.

Burns said the United States had had disputes with the Iranian government for many years, "but we don't have any arguments with the people of Iran. The people of Iran obviously are in need of support."
The United States was "shocked and saddened" to see the devastating effect the earthquake had on the Iranian people, he said.
Up to 2,400 people were killed and 40,000 injured on Saturday when an earthquake devastated some 200 villages in a rural area in eastern Iran, state media in Iran said.
The quake struck with a force of 7.1 on the Richter scale. It was Iran's most severe earthquake since 1990 when a quake killed more than 35,000 people.

The United States has no diplomatic relations with Iran, which it considers a pariah state guilty of sponsoring terrorism, sabotaging the Middle East peace process and developing nuclear and other weapons of mass destruction.
It has imposed a tough trade embargo on Iran and has repeatedly urged its friends and allies to follow suit.
Burns insisted that despite the willingness to help out in a humanitarian emergency, "we're going to maintain our policy of containment and isolation of Iran."
Last March, when another earthquake occurred in Iran, the United States gave $25,000 in emergency aid, Burns said.
Meanwhile, U.N. agencies were reported on Monday to have pledged $360,000 to Iran's earthquake victims, beginning with a $50,000 cash grant from the Department of Humanitarian Affairs.

According to a U.N. list, Japan was contributing $280,000 worth of supplies, including tents, blankets and flashlights, and Britain has contributed about $160,000 through the Red Cross to purchase supplies locally.
